meaning: something that is very easy to do
example: The test was a piece of cake, so I finished in ten minutes.
origin: The exact origin is unclear. One idea is that a slice of cake is an easy and pleasant thing to get.

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning of the words, not the idiomatic one.

wrong_meanings.meaning: something that is very difficult to do
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the real meaning. The idiom describes a task that is easy.
The idiom has nothing to do with celebrations. It is only about how easy a task is.

explanation: 'Piece of cake' is an informal expression that means something is very easy. People often use it to talk about tests, exercises or simple jobs.
